findings.text: follow-on: in the ascending sweep `~split_wall` also suppresses `terminal`, so a wall vertex that is the global maximum of the field would be dropped from the split tree (its `signed_maximum` node is never emitted, `connect` false and no arc); no fixture in the suite reaches it because the maximum sits interior on the 21x21 carriers and on the diverted production carrier, and the oracle could not see it anyway, as its last-vertex branch at tests/test_contour_tree_wall_split.py:202 asserts nothing.

follow-on: `assert 447 in wall_merges` pins a raw carrier vertex index, so a regenerated or reordered carrier fails here as a stale pin rather than as a topology regression and no message distinguishes the two; the oracle loop above it already carries the diagnostic tuple. A named lookup for the wall merge, or a message naming the expected vertex, would keep the guard informative.
